new_results.statement: For sigma A0[S,S]>=kappa I3 and arbitrary E, if beta1 is the largest eigenvalue of P_S (sigma E)_- P_S^T and beta1<kappa, then the full ambient form has a continuous density with supnorm <=6 sqrt(pi)/(kappa-beta1). Favorable spectral directions cost zero.

Under the same core assumption, if beta2 is the second eigenvalue of the hostile compression and beta2<kappa, then the full ambient form has essentially bounded density <=C*/(kappa-beta2), C*=24.183038289961516. The largest hostile compressed direction is completely free.
For H>=0 and physical triple S, there exists rank-one 0<=R<=H whose S-compression removes exactly the top eigencomponent of H[S,S], leaving operator norm equal to the second compressed eigenvalue.
